## What is this

<!-- New plugin submission, a new release for an existing plugin, a yank, a
     provider code registration, or a catalog infrastructure change? -->

## Checklist

- [ ] I ran `node scripts/validate.mjs` locally and it passes.
- [ ] I did **not** hand-edit `v1/index.json` (it is generated by
      `scripts/build-index.mjs` / `.github/workflows/build-index.yml`).
- [ ] JSON files are pretty-printed with 2-space indentation and end with a
      trailing newline (matches `.editorconfig`).

### If this adds or updates a `plugins/<id>.json`

- [ ] `download_url` (portable package), and/or each
      `downloads[<platform>]`'s `url`, point at a real GitHub Release asset.
      At least one of `download_url` or `downloads` is present, and every
      `downloads` key is also listed in `platforms`.
- [ ] `sha256` (portable and/or per-platform) matches its asset.
- [ ] Every package carries `plugin.sums` and `plugin.sums.minisig` at its
      root (see `docs/signing.md`), and a `community` entry has the
      `author_public_key` that signed them.
- [ ] Any new `dns01` provider `code` is registered in `codes.json` (run
      `node scripts/generate-codes.mjs <path-to-plugin.json>`).

### If this yanks a release

- [ ] Only `"yanked": true` was added to the affected `releases[]` entry —
      the entry itself was not deleted.
- [ ] The reason is described below (link a security advisory instead of
      exploit details for anything actively exploitable).
